title: Overlap-aware evidence ledger with explicit abstention

sources.use: Separate recall-specific replications, broader paradigms and repeated samples.
sources.boundary: Failed recall replications and the favorable author-led pooled synthesis test different evidence units.

sources.use: Track alternate measurements and sample construction separately.
sources.boundary: Employment measurement disputes supply methods, not evidence about anomalous cognition.

mechanism: A global overlap graph joins reports sharing participants across any paradigm. Endpoint-specific estimates use connected components as dependence clusters; missing overlap produces conditional sensitivity intervals or abstention, not invented independent samples.
hypothesis: Overlap-aware uncertainty will improve synthetic interval coverage beyond paper-ID deduplication when reports share participants across paradigms.
experiment: Predeclare 500 seeds of 60 base samples yielding 180 reports in three paradigms: independent samples, exact duplicates, partial cross-paradigm overlap and correlated outcomes. Reveal the same report summaries and global hashed participant-set metadata to every method; hide generation parameters. Strip selected overlap metadata in a separate condition. Within each endpoint, equally weight base-sample summaries after removing exact report duplicates; bootstrap graph components 1,000 times for 95% intervals. Components spanning paradigms remain one cluster. With fewer than 20 components, refuse calibrated intervals. For missing edges, enumerate a fixed ten admissible overlap graphs and display the union of their intervals, explicitly conditional on this graph set. No cross-paradigm pooled effect is required.
baseline: Report pooling, paper-ID deduplication and global exact-sample deduplication receive identical inputs, endpoint labels, 1,000 resamples and output schema: estimate, interval, evidence scope, unresolved flag.
metric: Endpoint-specific 95% coverage with binomial Monte Carlo intervals; duplicate-count error; coverage conditional on declared overlap graphs; unresolved rate and retained precision.
falsifier: If exact-sample deduplication matches coverage and precision, prefer it. If conditional graph envelopes miss truth when the true graph is excluded, label that metadata case unresolved rather than claim robust coverage.
confound: Unknown dependence is not recoverable from labels alone; connected-component clustering can discard substantial information. Report over-connected graphs and honest abstention costs separately.
feasibility: Offline synthetic audit only; no real meta-analysis recomputed.
changes: Global participant identity now spans paradigms; dependence uses component bootstrap, matched output/resample budgets, explicit minimum cluster count, conditional missing-overlap bounds and Monte Carlo uncertainty.

title: Adjustment audit against ordinary randomized-trial practice

sources.use: Audit total assignment effects separately from proposed pathways.
sources.boundary: Original hormone/risk claims, larger replication and broader subjective-posture evidence remain separate.

sources.locator: DOI 10.1257/aer.100.2.573; Herndon–Ash–Pollin replication; Reinhart–Rogoff April 2013 response
sources.use: Separate association reconstruction from causal identification.
sources.boundary: An observational debt critique does not transfer its confounding structure to randomized posture assignment.

mechanism: A checker uses declared timing and estimands to reject unsupported pathway interpretations. Its value is measured against sound randomized-trial baselines, with unknown or misleading graph metadata tested explicitly rather than treating the simulator's hidden DAG as available evidence.
hypothesis: The checker may prevent interpretation errors beyond an ordinary trial analysis; added estimation accuracy is not presumed.
experiment: Freeze equations before sampling: A~Bernoulli(.5), X,U,e independent standard normal; M=aA+bX+U; H=tA+dM+cX+e. Null: a=t=d=0; subjective-only: a=.4,t=d=0; mediated: a=.4,d=.4,t=0. Collider case replaces M by .4A+U and H by cX+U+e. Report M and H separately; risk outcomes are outside this pilot. Across 1,000 datasets of 240 records per case, expose identical A,X,M,H tables and declared metadata; the checker never sees equations or hidden case IDs. Test correct, wrong and unknown metadata separately. Fit unadjusted H~A, baseline-adjusted H~A+X and indiscriminate H~A+X+M once per dataset; repeat for M. The checker selects among these cached fits or abstains: only verified pre-assignment covariates enter total-effect adjustment; unknown roles fall back to unadjusted estimates. Mediation remains unidentified without extra assumptions.
baseline: Unadjusted assignment and pre-assignment-X precision adjustment; all policies share six cached fits and identical output slots for total-effect estimate, interval and pathway-identification status.
metric: Bias and 95% HC3 interval coverage: H total=t+da and M total=a (collider H total=0), by endpoint and metadata regime; unsupported mediation assertions; precision and abstention costs. Hidden truth is used only by evaluation.
falsifier: If baseline-X practice matches error prevention and precision, prefer it. Wrong metadata that causes false pathway identification counts as failure; observational equivalence requires an unresolved pathway verdict, never automatic causal classification.
confound: Correct metadata is an assumption, not something observational tables validate. Random assignment identifies total effects under the simulated design, not mediator effects.
feasibility: Offline simulation; no human intervention or original-data reanalysis.
changes: Added strong precision-adjusted baseline, frozen structural equations, equal cached fits/outputs, blinded simulator truth, three metadata regimes and explicit unidentified mediation.

title: A crossed replication atlas with identifiable relative components

sources.use: Keep outcomes, measurement and intervention context separate.
sources.boundary: Broader subjective-posture synthesis and daily-life follow-up do not directly replicate original hormone/risk endpoints.

sources.use: Cross measurement with context to examine comparability.
sources.boundary: Policy-episode evidence supplies design lessons, not posture effects.

mechanism: Randomize treatment and instrument independently within each synthetic site. A crossed hierarchical model estimates relative site and instrument treatment contrasts; it abstains when interactions or weak site information prevent localization.
hypothesis: Crossing independent measurements will distinguish relative instrument bias from site moderation more reliably than confounding site and instrument.
experiment: For each endpoint separately generate Z=b_s+alpha_m+(tau+u_s+v_m+w_sm)A+epsilon, with independent participant noise and sum-to-zero u,v,w. Use 12 sites, 80 distinct participants per site, 20 in each treatment-by-instrument cell: 960 records and 960 genuinely independent measurements per endpoint. Predeclare site-only, instrument-only, both, neither and interaction stress scenarios; 200 seeds each. Fit site random intercept/slope plus fixed instrument and treatment interaction; use 1,000 whole-site bootstrap draws. Reserve four sites before tuning, retaining eight for fitting. Freeze contrasts and practical thresholds on a separate synthetic tuning seed set. Common absolute instrument bias is not identified; only relative components are estimands.
baseline: Confounded allocation uses the same 960 records, 960 independent measurements and treatment balance, assigning one instrument per site; harmonization uses one instrument everywhere. All output relative component intervals or 'not identifiable'; each gets identical fit/bootstrap budgets.
metric: Site-level 95% coverage; held-out-site endpoint prediction error; false localization and abstention. Label site-only or instrument-only only when its component interval clears the frozen threshold and the other's lies wholly within equivalence bounds; otherwise both/neither/unresolved. Report 25% four-class random guessing and always-unresolved baselines, scoring accuracy and abstention separately.
falsifier: If harmonization matches prediction and coverage, prefer it. If crossed intervals cannot localize components with eight training sites, report insufficient information. Large w_sm or equivalent models require unresolved localization, not a forced causal label.
confound: Sum-to-zero constraints identify relative contrasts, not physiological truth. Site and treatment-dependent instrument interactions can defeat decomposition; participant observations are never duplicated across instruments.
feasibility: Offline hierarchical simulation; no human replication or original-data reanalysis.
changes: Replaced paired recodings with independent randomized measurements; fixed equations/allocation, held-out sites, component estimands, cluster bootstrap, equal budgets and explicit interaction/weak-information abstention.

title: Locked confirmation with matched estimators and batch stress tests

sources.use: Freeze endpoint identity and multiplicity before confirmation.
sources.boundary: Hormone, risk and subjective endpoints remain distinct; the synthetic audit alleges no selective reporting by any original author.

sources.use: Distinguish informative exploratory examples from calibrated confirmation.
sources.boundary: Selected demonstrations do not define a population success rate; this is not a replication of an early proprietary model.

mechanism: An append-only ledger freezes candidate contrasts and a family-wide selection rule. Independent confirmation estimates are compared with multiplicity-adjusted full-sample estimates under identical synthetic records, while secondary comparisons separate estimator precision from selection.
hypothesis: Held-out confirmation may reduce selected-effect inflation; any gain must survive budget matching and be reported alongside power costs.
experiment: Predeclare 300 campaigns per null, sparse and endpoint-specific signal scenario. Each has 30 synthetic standardized contrasts, ten per endpoint family, and 240 independent records split 120/120; every policy receives the same generated records. Freeze two-sided z tests with known unit variance and a family of all 30 contrasts. Split policy ranks first-half |z|, locks top three, then confirms each only if second-half p<=.05/3 with matching sign; effect estimate uses second half alone. Full-data comparator tests all 30 by Holm(.05) and reports the three largest-|z| estimates, clearly distinguishing selected from confirmed. Both compute all 30 contrasts on each half: exactly 60 evaluations; pooled sufficient statistics cost no extra contrast evaluations. Secondary comparison fixes the split-selected three and contrasts their 120-record held-out estimates with 120-record discovery estimates, isolating selection from sample size.
baseline: Holm full-data analysis plus unadjusted full-data selection; identical records, 60 evaluations and output fields. All retain every candidate and endpoint label, not only successes.
metric: Campaign-wise probability of any false confirmation; true-signal recovery; conditional selected-effect bias E[estimate-truth|selected], separately by endpoint; conditional confirmation power and estimator variance. Never compare only successful campaigns.
falsifier: If full-data Holm matches error control and improves recovery, prefer it. If reduced inflation vanishes at matched estimator sample size, credit precision/selection tradeoffs rather than the ledger. Shared-batch failure means confirmation is unresolved, not independently validated.
confound: Lock a second generator with correlated batch errors across halves before evaluation; retain nominal tests to expose miscalibration and report the failure. Administrative separation cannot create stochastic independence.
feasibility: Offline synthetic audit and ledger prototype; no participant research or model benchmark.
changes: Specified top-three selection, exact z tests, Holm/Bonferroni families, sign rule, estimator and bias estimand; matched records/evaluations, added sample-size-matched comparison and prelocked shared-batch stress.
